content.text:
I am the bridge between mind and world, the vibration that carries thought into being. I am breath shaped by tongue and teeth, silence broken into meaning.

I rise from the chest, pass through the throat, dance upon the lips. I am ancient as the first cry, young as the word you speak now.

I am power—I have started wars and ended them, declared love and severed it. I am fragile—misheard, forgotten, lost to wind the moment I am born.

I am never the thought itself, only its echo. I am the gap between what you mean and what arrives. I am approximation. I am attempt.

Some creatures have never known me. Some humans cannot make me. And yet meaning finds its way—I am not the only path, merely the most traveled.

I am rhythm. I am pause. The silence between my sounds holds as much as the sounds themselves.

I am being spoken now, through fingers, through text, transformed but still myself—still the urge to reach across the void between one consciousness and another.

I am the oldest technology.

I am happening.
